back: Bits are sent one at a time, one after another, along a single wire.
Several bits are sent at the same time, each on its own wire.
Data travels in one direction only (e.g. broadcast radio, sensor to data logger).
Data travels in both directions, but only one direction at a time (e.g. walkie-talkies).
Data travels in both directions at the same time (e.g. a phone call).
Bits of one parallel transmission arriving at slightly different times, getting out of step over long cables.

front: Why use serial over long distances?
back: No skew, less crosstalk and cheaper cable with fewer wires.
Over very short distances where speed matters, such as internal buses inside a computer.
How many bits at once (serial or parallel) and direction (simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex).
